Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-d850b495 — extend diagonal colored rays

Use when this task recurs with a sparse, multicolor cluster near a corner/edge and a uniform background.

## Rule established by demonstrations and accepted test
The input contains short same-color diagonal line segments (often two cells) that are parts of longer rays. Extend each such segment linearly in both its detected diagonal orientation and color until the grid boundary, preserving the given cells and all unrelated cells. The demonstrated/accepted cases place each ray's existing cells at the inward end, so the new cells continue outward from the outermost segment cell in the same diagonal direction. Different colors use independent diagonal rays; do not fill other parts of the grid.

Demonstration evidence:
- A two-cell color-1 down-right diagonal continued down-right to the border.
- A two-cell color-8 down-left diagonal continued down-left to the border.
- In the accepted test for this task, rays continued along diagonals for colors 6 (up-left), 3 (up-right), 0 (down-left), and 8 (down-right), each until the respective edge.

## Procedure
1. Read the fresh grid and identify its uniform background and colored cells.
2. Group same-color cells by diagonal direction (constant row-column or row+column). A short collinear segment establishes a ray; infer its outward direction from its placement/orientation in the source cluster.
3. Extend only evidenced rays to the grid boundary, preserving all existing cells. Do not automatically extend isolated cells unless cluster geometry supports them.
4. Validate dimensions, bounds, and each emitted ray's color and diagonal alignment.

## Recurrence clarification (2026-09)
Do not assume that every apparent short line or multicolor cluster should extend. A 6x12 demo containing a 2x2 cluster at the right edge with background 8 and colors 0, 1, 6, 9 remained completely unchanged. Another demo with background 9 and a short color-3 down-right diagonal, plus colors 0 and 1 nearby, extended only the color-3 diagonal backward/up-left to the top-left boundary; other cells were unchanged. A separate demo extended color-8 from its near-bottom vertical-ish source arrangement up-right to the top-right boundary, while leaving color-0 cells untouched. The accepted test was a no-op: its 2x2 pattern at rows 0-1, cols 9-10 contained four distinct colors (3,1;2,5), and output preserved it with background 8. Thus the selector is unresolved/context-dependent; explicitly detect whether an evidenced repeated-color diagonal ray exists and do not extrapolate a ray from a 2x2 patch of distinct colors. When only distinct-color adjacency is present, preserving the input can be correct.

## Caution
Source clusters may vary across recurring inputs. Infer each ray from the current grid rather than memorizing coordinates or palette.
